name: Kachari Ruins (Ruins of Kachari Rajbari)
description: Medieval ruins of the ancient Dimasa Kachari kingdom capital in Dimapur, featuring distinctive mushroom-domed sandstone pillars and carved monoliths dating to the 10th-13th centuries.
facts: Ancient capital of the Dimasa Kachari kingdom before Ahom invasion.
Features mushroom-shaped pillars carved with birds, animals and motifs.
Maintained by Archaeological Survey of India.
Located behind Naga Shopping Arcade in Dimapur town.
Best visited October to March.

name: Diezephe Craft Village
description: Handicraft village renowned for traditional Naga woodcarving, bamboo and cane work, and loinloom weaving, with artisan workshops, museum and Weaver’s Place homestay.
facts: Home to skilled weavers and craftsmen of Tenyimei/Chakhesang communities.
Promoted by Nagaland Handloom and Handicrafts Development Corporation.
Hosts annual International Loinloom Festival in early December.
About 13 km from Dimapur; now primarily in Chümoukedima district.
Recognized as Best Tourism Village 2023.

name: NEZCC Stone Garden and Museum
description: North East Zone Cultural Centre complex featuring a stone sculpture garden with works by Indian artists, traditional morungs, amphitheatre and Northeast Heritage Museum.
facts: Showcases 31 stone sculptures by artists from across India.
Houses North East Heritage Museum with crafts from eight NE states.
Located near Dimapur Airport, about 3 km from railway station.
Includes children’s park and hanging bridge.
Open for cultural programmes and public visits.

name: Green Park
description: Landscaped family park within the State Horticulture Nursery at 4th Mile, Dimapur, offering boating, ziplining, water zorbing, kids train and picnic spots amid greenery.
facts: Located inside State Horticulture Nursery grounds.
Features adventure activities and restaurant.
Nominal entry fee; popular for picnics.
Best time October to March.
Easily accessible from Dimapur city centre.

name: Nagaland Zoological Park
description: State’s main zoo at Rangapahar spanning 176 hectares, housing native Northeast Indian fauna including hornbills, hoolock gibbon, tigers and other species; part of Rangapahar Wildlife Sanctuary.
facts: Opened in 2008; closed on Mondays.
Focuses on Northeast Indian biodiversity with ~40 species.
Located about 6-8 km from Dimapur; now in Chümoukedima district.
Entry fee applies; ideal for families.
Adjacent to Rangapahar Reserve Forest for birdwatching.

name: Triple Falls (Seithekima)
description: Scenic three-tier waterfall near Seithekima village cascading about 280 feet into natural pools, surrounded by lush forest; popular for picnics, photography and light trekking.
facts: Three distinct streams forming a natural spectacle.
About 18-26 km from central Dimapur.
Managed with tourism support; best post-monsoon.
Approach involves short trek through greenery.
Note: area associated with Chümoukedima district.

name: Dimapur Town
description: Largest city and commercial gateway of Nagaland on the Dhansiri River plains, serving as the primary entry point with airport, railway station and bustling markets reflecting Naga and multi-ethnic culture.
facts: Only major plains city in hilly Nagaland.
Key rail and air hub for the state.
Historic Kachari capital area.
Vibrant markets including Hong Kong Market for handicrafts and goods.
Requires Inner Line Permit for visitors from outside Nagaland.

name: Hong Kong Market
description: Bustling flea market in central Dimapur known for imported and local goods, clothing, electronics, and Naga handicrafts; a lively commercial hub popular with locals and tourists.
facts: One of Dimapur’s most famous markets.
Sells traditional Naga garments, bamboo crafts and everyday items.
Central location near major transport points.
Best explored during daytime.

name: Zunheboto Town
description: District headquarters of Zünheboto, known as the Land of Warriors, a high-altitude Sumi Naga town at about 1,852 m offering panoramic views, traditional culture and access to nearby nature sites.
facts: Inhabited primarily by Sumi Nagas; named after a flowering shrub on the hilltop.
Elevation around 1,850 m with cool climate.
Gateway to Satoi Range and Ghosu Bird Sanctuary.
Hosts Tuluni and Ahuna festivals.
Requires Inner Line Permit for non-residents.

name: Sümi Baptist Church, Zünheboto
description: One of the largest church buildings in Asia, a monumental Baptist church dominating Zunheboto skyline with capacity for 8,500 worshippers, blue dome and white turrets, completed in 2017.
facts: Founded 1942; new building dedicated 22 April 2017 after 10 years of construction.
Seating capacity over 8,500; height 166 feet.
Bell imported from Poland; cost about ₹36 crore.
Affiliated with Nagaland Baptist Church Council.
Iconic viewpoint for the town.

name: Ghosu Bird Sanctuary
description: Community-conserved bird sanctuary about 8-12 km from Zunheboto near Ghukiye, protecting over 20 endangered bird species and hosting migratory birds June-September; maintained by local villages.
facts: Home to Spot-breasted Laughingthrush, hornbills and migratory pigeons/doves.
Features a natural salt lick important for wildlife.
Established as community conservation area around 2014 by Ghukiye and Nikuto villages.
Best for birdwatching May-September.
Tourist lodge available nearby; about 8 km from town.

name: Satoi Range
description: Pristine virgin cloud forest ridge in southern Zunheboto rising over 2,200 m, one of the last habitats for Blyth’s Tragopan, endemic rhododendrons and rock caves used as ancestral shelters.
facts: Important Bird Area and Endemic Bird Area of India.
Habitat of Blyth’s Tragopan (state bird), kalij pheasant and others.
Rhododendrons bloom April-May; ideal for camping and trekking.
Surrounded by about 10 villages of Satakha sub-division.
Access limited; best with local guides.

name: Pughoboto Town
description: Historic town and oldest sub-division in Zunheboto district, ancestral home of the Sumi Nagas on the foothills of Mt. Puhukito amid oak forests; gateway linking Kohima and Zunheboto.
facts: Sumi Nagas originated here; Christianity first entered nearby Ighanumi village.
Elevation about 1,350 m; known for Green Pughoboto initiatives.
About 60-85 km from Zunheboto and Kohima.
Offers views of Doyang river valley and access to nearby villages.
Administrative and cultural hub for western Zunheboto.

name: Aizuto Forest and Area
description: Scenic forested area near Aizuto village in Zunheboto district with dense vegetation, picnic potential and proximity to mission centres; part of the district’s wildlife and nature attractions.
facts: Mentioned among wildlife reserves and picnic spots in tourism guides.
Near Aizuto Mission Centre.
Elevated location with cool climate.
Suitable for nature walks and birdwatching.
About 20-25 km from Zunheboto town.

name: Sukhai-Kivikhu-Sheshemi Eco-Circuit
description: Pioneering community-based tourism circuit of neighbouring Sumi villages that have banned hunting and tree-cutting, offering traditional morung replicas, guided forest trails and authentic homestays.
facts: Part of Tizu Valley Biodiversity Conservation and Livelihood Network.
Villages include Sukhai, Kivikhu and others practising sustainable practices.
Opportunities for forest trails, cultural immersion and birdwatching.
Supports local youth volunteers and homestays.
Located south of Zunheboto near Satakha area.

name: Tizu River (Zunheboto Section)
description: Major river flowing through Zunheboto district, one of the three main rivers (with Doyang and Tsutha) adding scenic charm to the valleys and supporting community conservation efforts.
facts: One of the principal rivers of the district.
Associated with Tizu Valley community conservation sites.
Offers scenic views and potential for nature activities.
Flows through multiple villages and forested areas.
Best experienced with local guidance.
